The fix is correct. NetworksHandler.read delegates to NetworksListingForm.filter_subnets, which returns `subnets.order_by("id")` (src/maasserver/forms/__init__.py:2267), so the response is ordered numerically by subnet id, not lexicographically by the rendered "subnet-<id>" name. The old assertion only passed while string sort and numeric sort coincided (ids with equal digit counts), which broke at the 99→100 boundary. Sorting the expected values by `subnet.id` matches the actual API behavior. One residual nit: the test is named `test_GET_sorts_by_name`, but it has never exercised name-based sorting — the endpoint orders by id. Consider renaming it to `test_GET_sorts_by_id` (line 93, outside this hunk) so the name doesn't mislead the next reader into "fixing" the assertion back to name order.

src/maasserver/api/tests/test_networks.p.104: Correct expectation: the handler orders by subnet id (filter_subnets does `subnets.order_by("id")`), not by the "subnet-<id>" name string. While here, consider renaming the test from `test_GET_sorts_by_name` to `test_GET_sorts_by_id` — the current name describes behavior the API never had and invites regressions of this same fix.
